$comment: The patch-set record. This is the budget for local divergence from upstream: docs/ELECTRON_APP_PLAN.md §1. A7 in scripts/verify-bundles.mjs diffs core/ and lib/ against upstreamRef and fails the build if the changed file set differs from patchedFiles. Deliberate new patches must be added here; accidental edits must not be.

patches.summary: Drop the up-front JID normalisation, add receipt/received/played blocking, move JID derivation into the switch.
patches.note: Local fix for chats appearing read despite receipt blocking (LID change on WhatsApp's side). Not yet sent upstream.

patches.summary: Delete the isOutgoingMessage = innerHTML.includes('aria-label="You:"') override that broke device badges.

patches.why: interception.js:28 and ui.js:18 both declared and called a top-level `initialize`. Concatenating the two bundles makes the LAST declaration win for the whole script, so interception.js silently called ui.js's version, the WebSocket hook never armed, and nothing errored. Verified: ui.js's `initialize` is referenced nowhere else and never re-invoked, so the rename is safe.

patches.summary: Gate both checkNodeEncoderSanity calls and the byte-compare behind WAdebugMode.
patches.why: checkNodeEncoderSanity did a full decodeStanza + encodeStanza + isEqualArray on every inbound AND outbound frame, purely as a developer self-check, then isEqualArray ran a second time to decide whether to hit `debugger`. Dev-only work on the hot path.
patches.note: WAdebugMode still exposes the full self-check for anyone debugging.

patches.file: core/interception.js, core/multi_device.js, core/utils.js, core/ui.js, core/parsing/binary_reader.js, core/parsing/node_reader_writer.js
patches.summary: Remove 15 live `debugger;` statements (13 removed + 1 inline guard rewritten + 1 removed as part of P3).
patches.why: A `debugger` statement is free with no debugger attached but SUSPENDS execution when DevTools is open. Electron users will open DevTools. The worst sites were interception.js:74 and :703 (every outbound frame) and hookedPromiseError (every unhandled promise rejection anywhere in WhatsApp, installed by default because WALogs = true).
patches.note: Applied by scripts/apply-p4-debugger.mjs, which only touches lines that are exactly `debugger;` and leaves `//debugger;` comments alone. Idempotent.

patches.summary: Hoist `isIncoming` to a declared local in wsHook.before/after instead of assigning it inline at 6 call sites.
patches.why: `isIncoming` was never declared anywhere in the file, so every `isIncoming=false` / `isIncoming=true` argument was an implicit global write — on the per-frame path. The values were correct, but the pattern is a landmine and pollutes the global namespace.

patches.summary: Re-encode the two protobuf files UTF-16 -> UTF-8 (halving them), and strip the UTF-8 BOM from core/ui.js, core/ui_class_names.js and background.js.
patches.why: The UTF-16 -> UTF-8 re-encode is pre-existing (commit 10809c8) and roughly halved the two protobuf files, which is why the byte figures in the plan are ~1.3 MB rather than ~2.6 MB for the main bundle. The BOM strip is new: a BOM is legal JS mid-script but is not something to rely on at a concatenation seam, and it breaks JSON.parse ahead of a JSON literal. The build also strips BOMs on read (scripts/build.mjs readSource) and assertion A10 guards both source and output.
patches.note: background.js still differs from upstream for this reason but is not inside core/ or lib/, so it is not part of the A7 diff.

patches.summary: Make hookLogs()'s WALogger installation resolve with a bounded retry and a null-safe rebuildTemplate, instead of a single unguarded call 2s after injection.
patches.why: Observed at runtime on every launch: 'Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading LOG)'. `require("WALogger")` returns null until WhatsApp's webpack bundle registers that module, and upstream ran the install once at a fixed 2s delay with no guard, inside a setTimeout, so the throw was uncaught AND then surfaced through the window.onunhandledrejection hook installed immediately above it.
patches.extraFix: P7b: `originalWALoggerDev` was assigned `.LOG` instead of `.DEV`, so hookedWALoggerDev invoked the log function's original with DEV arguments.
patches.note: Applied by scripts/apply-p7-walogger.mjs (idempotent, line-range based). The log hook exists to stop WhatsApp's own error reports leaking, so it still installs — it just no longer throws when the module is not ready yet, and it gives up quietly after ~20s rather than throwing on the page.

patches.summary: Scope the body-level MutationObserver, short-circuit non-element nodes, and gate the one-shot `getElementsByClassName('two')` probe behind a uiReady flag.
patches.why: ui.js:40 observes document.body with {childList, subtree} and onMutationsObserved calls getElementsByClassName('two') on EVERY added node, which walks that node's whole subtree. Cost is O(mutations x subtree size) and is the dominant steady-state CPU cost — and the dominant cost while the app sits hidden in the tray, because a backgrounded WhatsApp session still churns (other chats' presence, typing indicators, preview updates).
patches.gate: MUST pass the full feature parity matrix (docs §10) before shipping. This is the only patch that changes WHEN UI work happens, so treat a regression as a release blocker.
patches.note: ui.js is already in the patch set via P0b, so this adds no new merge-conflict domain.

encoding.$comment: core/parsing/protobuf/{WAProto,WhisperTextProtocol}.js were re-encoded UTF-16 -> UTF-8 by commit 10809c8, which halved them. core/ui.js and background.js still carry a UTF-8 BOM. These are not behavioural patches but they do appear in the diff, so they are declared here rather than left as a surprise.
